body:
5.14 "that the application is not susceptible XPath injection" -> "that the application is not susceptible to XPath injection"

5.27 and 5.30 are the same

I would suggest adding additional deserialization-related requirements instead of just 5.29: "Verify that deserialization of untrusted data is avoided or is extensively protected when deserialization cannot be avoided."

For example:

5.29 "Verify that deserialization of untrusted data is avoided. The secure use of other formats such as JSON is recommended."

5.30 "If deserialization is used, encryption and hashing controls should be used to ensure no tampering is permitted by untrusted sources.  These checks should be performed before deserialization.  If this  is not an option, mechanisms to ensure that only specific object types are deserialized such as LAOIS should be used"

Should we also mention deserialization DoS based attacks as well (although there really aren't any good protections against this)?

We can also add links to the Deserialization related resources - see https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/262

comments.body: Please review the current version; I've made quite substantial refactoring to include input validation, output encoding, injection prevention, and then deserialization. There's a strong case for buffer overflows and so on to be their own section as well. Check it out and let me know.
Addressed in @vanderaj and did a little cleanup here. If anything you need persists please open new issue.
